MARKING SCHEME
MEDIA TECHNOLOGY
GRADE: 10 (SENIOR SCHOOL)
SECTION A (30 MARKS)
 (a) Identify: Newspaper (Print Media). (1mk)
 (b) Name: Billboard. (1mk)
 (c) Distinguish: Traditional media refers to legacy formats like newspapers, radio, and TV that have a one-way
 flow of information (3mks). New media refers to digital, interactive, and internet-based platforms like social
 media and streaming services that allow real-time feedback.
 (a) (i) X: Lens (Zoom or Prime). (1mk)
 (ii) Y: Shutter Release Button. (1mk)
 (b) Function: Allows the photographer to see the exact frame and composition that the lens is capturing before
 taking the picture. (2mks)
 (c) True/False: TRUE. (1mk)
 (a) — (ii)
 (b) — (i)
 (c) — (iv)
 (d) — (iii)
 (e) — (v) (1 mark each)
 (a) Identify: Condenser Microphone (or Shotgun Microphone). (1mk)
 (b) Accessories: Boom pole, Windjammer (Deadcat), or Microphone Stand. (2mks)
 (c) Ambience: The background or atmospheric sounds of a specific location (e.g., birds chirping in a forest) that
 give the recording a sense of place. (2mks)
 (a) Ownership Types: Private-owned, Community-owned, Government-owned. (3mks)
 (b) Advantages: Promotes local culture/language and addresses specific community needs that national media
 might ignore. (2mks)
 (c) Roles: (i) Finance Officer/Accountant, (ii) Editor or Art Director. (2mks)
 (d) Legal Advisor: Ensures the company complies with media laws (like defamation or copyright), handles
 contracts, and advises on censorship issues. (3mks)
SECTION B (50 MARKS)
 (a) Phase: Pre-production. (1mk)
 (b) Steps: Scriptwriting, Budgeting, Casting, Scheduling/Location Scouting. (4mks)
 (c) Research: Helps in understanding the target audience, finding accurate facts about conservation in Kwale, and
 determining the best setting/characters to make the film believable. (4mks)
 (d) Flow Chart: (6mks)
 Pre-production (Ideation & Planning)
 Production (Filming & Sound Recording)
 Post-production (Editing & Distribution)
 (a) Hazards: Trailing cables (tripping hazard), overloaded sockets (fire hazard), hot lights near flammable
 materials. (3mks)
 (b) Mitigation: Tape down cables using gaffer tape, use cable protectors, and ensure sockets are not overloaded
 using surge protectors. (3mks)
 (c) Comparison: A Tripod is a stationary three-legged stand for stable, fixed shots; a Gimbal is a motorized
 stabilizer that allows for smooth, fluid movement while the camera is being carried. (4mks)
 (d) Sound Operator: Responsible for capturing clean dialogue and preventing "clipping" or background noise
 interference during filming. (2mks)
 (e) Cleaning Kit: Lens blower, Microfiber cloth, Lens cleaning solution/pen. (3mks)
 (a) Software: Filmora. (1mk)
 (b) Steps: Importing is the process of bringing raw footage into the editing software. Exporting is the final step
 where the edited project is rendered into a playable file format (e.g., MP4). (4mks)
 (c) Editor Role: Selects the best takes, cuts footage to maintain rhythm, adds transitions, and syncs audio with
 video. (3mks)
 (d) Disadvantage: Limited processing power for high-resolution 4K files and fewer advanced tools for complex
 sound mixing or VFX. (2mks)
 (a) Genres: A: Wildlife, B: Street Photography, C: Portraiture. (3mks)
 (b) Photojournalism: Acts as a "watchdog" for society by documenting truth, historical events, and social issues
 to inform the public. (3mks)
 (c) Accessories: Telephoto lens (to shoot from a distance) and a Tripod/Monopod for stability. (2mks)
 (d) Ethics: Obtaining Informed Consent before taking and publishing a photo of an individual. (2mks)
